# Nelson Frank — Fullstack Engineer

Nelson Frank is a fullstack engineer building secure auth, transit backends, and cloud infrastructure with TypeScript, Go, and Python on Kubernetes. Based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, working with teams worldwide.

## Core Profile
- **Website URL**: https://nelsonfrank.dev
- **Main Stack**: TypeScript, Go, Python, Next.js, NestJS, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes.
- **RSS Feed**: https://nelsonfrank.dev/feed.xml

## Site Structure

- [Home](https://nelsonfrank.dev/) — Overview, selected work, recent writing, experience summary, and contact.
- [Projects](https://nelsonfrank.dev/projects) — Engineering case studies and architecture write-ups.
- [Writing](https://nelsonfrank.dev/writing) — Technical articles and deep dives.
- [Experience](https://nelsonfrank.dev/experience) — Work history and engineering roles.

## Featured Projects

- [Passkey Authentication Engine](https://nelsonfrank.dev/projects/passkey-auth) — Biometric passwordless and multi-factor authentication system built with WebAuthn, NestJS, React, and PostgreSQL (`Browser -> NestJS API -> Postgres`).
- [City Connector Backend](https://nelsonfrank.dev/projects/city-connector-backend) — High-performance transit routing (RAPTOR) and real-time GTFS engine built with Go, Python, Kong Gateway, Redis, and Kubernetes (`Kong -> Go RAPTOR -> Redis`).
- [NECTA Explorer](https://nelsonfrank.dev/projects/necta-explorer) — Asynchronous Python web crawler and interactive Next.js analytics dashboard for Tanzania NECTA examination results (`Scraper -> Postgres -> Next.js`).

## Latest Articles

- [TOTP Authentication: How It Works and How It's Built](https://nelsonfrank.dev/writing/TOTP-authentication) — A ground-up explanation of OTP, HOTP, and TOTP with a full walkthrough of a production NestJS + React implementation.
- [Using Passkeys for Multi-Factor Authentication](https://nelsonfrank.dev/writing/passkey-auth-as-multi-factor-auth-option) — A deep dive into using passkeys and WebAuthn for phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.
- [Mastering TypeScript Generics](https://nelsonfrank.dev/writing/typescript-generics) — How generics make TypeScript code flexible, reusable, and type-safe.
